subject: Competitive bake-off recap - Redwood vs. OmniHealth
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap - Redwood vs. OmniHealth

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the demo so we have a single source of truth and clear next steps. Let me know if I missed anything.

Pain points you mentioned:
- High per-request latency on current LLM endpoints during peak hours (customer-facing chat).
- Need to reduce inference cost per 1k tokens to meet budget targets for Q3.
- Data residency and audit logs requirement for PHI-adjacent use cases.
- Concern about graceful degradation during traffic spikes and vendor fallbacks.

Goals / success criteria:
1) 95th percentile latency under 200ms for 256-token responses in production workloads.
2) Unit cost below $0.002/token for average session profiles (40 tokens/output).
3) SOC 2 + KMS support and audit log access for all calls.
4) Seamless canary/rollout behavior and predictable autoscaling.

Competitive landscape you told us you'll evaluate:
- Redwood (us): focused on production inference, autoscaling, KV caching.
- Weights & Co (competitor A): claims lower per-token cost but less mature rollouts.
- CloudAI Endpoints (competitor B): easy integration, but limited caching and high egress.

Proposed bake-off plan (attached redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf):
- 1-week controlled test using your staging traffic replay + synthetic hill-climb scenarios.
- Benchmark targets for latency, throughput (50 concurrent users), and cost.
- We will provide a signed non-prod test environment with a private model variant and audit logs.

Immediate next steps:
- I’ll send the bake-off plan and a minimum test dataset you can share internally (attached).
- Can we schedule the technical deep-dive (infra + security) next Wed or Thu (Feb 25–26)?
- Please confirm the list of people who need access to the test results and any additional acceptance criteria.

Thanks — looking forward to running this together.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf, omni_requirements.xlsx

From: Samir Patel <samir@omnihealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Leah Gomez <leah@omnihealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap - Redwood vs. OmniHealth

Thanks for the clear recap, Aditya — this matches our notes. A few clarifications and asks from our side: 

1) Decision criteria: Beyond latency and cost, our procurement team will weight
   - Data residency and auditability (must have KMS/HSM integration)
   - SLA: 99.9% uptime target with meaningful remedies
   - Integration effort (we prefer minimal SDK changes)

2) Test dataset: We can provide an anonymized staging replay. Will that be sufficient for latency/cost profiling? We also want to run a set of red-team prompts for hallucination checks.

3) Can you confirm which Redwood model variants you plan to use for the test (quantized vs fp16)? Also will the 95th percentile 200ms target be measured from our staging region (us-west-2)?

4) Timeline: Feb 25 technical deep-dive works for our infra and security leads. We’d like to invite both them and procurement.

If you can share the exact test harness and expected metrics output format, procurement can start drafting the evaluation matrix.

Samir
Director of AI Platforms | OmniHealth
samir@omnihealth.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap - Redwood vs. OmniHealth

Samir — great questions, thanks. Short answers inline, plus a few additions.

> 1) Decision criteria... KMS/HSM integration
We support KMS-based envelope encryption and can operate with customer-managed keys in our Dedicated and Private offerings. Audit logs with per-request metadata will be enabled for the bake-off.

> 2) Test dataset: anonymized staging replay OK?
Yes — staging replay works and is ideal for realistic latency profiling. For hallucination checks, please include your red-team prompt set as a separate file. We’ll run the same prompts across vendor runs.

> 3) Which model variants? 95th measured from us-west-2?
Plan: we’ll run the bake-off on our recommended quantized variant (q8) and a fp16 baseline so you can compare cost vs quality. We will measure 95th percentile from us-west-2 to match your staging region.

> 4) Timeline: Feb 25 deep-dive
Confirmed — we’ll schedule Feb 25, 10:00–11:30 PT for a technical deep-dive. I’ll pull in our infra engineer (Rishi) and product (Marissa). I’ll send a calendar invite after you confirm participants.

Test harness + metrics: attached is a short spec and an example CSV output for latency, p50/p95/p99, cost-per-1k-tokens, and hallucination score (see redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf).

Open question for you: does procurement require a signed NDA before we run vendor-provided scripts in your staging environment? We typically operate under a standard evaluation agreement — happy to have legal coordinate.

Next steps (action items):
- OmniHealth: confirm staging replay file and red-team prompts by Feb 23.
- Redwood: provide calendar invite for Feb 25 deep-dive and prep test harness.
- Procurement/legal: point person for the NDA?

Best,
Aditya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap - Redwood vs. OmniHealth

Internal notes (do not forward):

Quick competitive snapshot after listening to the call:
- Weights & Co: likely lower headline price but no KV cache and no per-request audit logs today — risk on auditability.
- CloudAI Endpoints: solid uptime but poor autoscaling for bursty chat patterns (observed in earlier tests).

Benchmark knobs to include in the bake-off (recommendation):
- 50 concurrent users, 25–75 token responses (avg 40).
- Two variants: q8 quantized and fp16 baseline.
- Measure both cold-start and steady-state p95; include breakdown of token types (prompt vs generation).
- Include a resiliency test: simulate 30% CPU/GPU throttling and check graceful fallback to smaller model variant.

Acceptance criteria suggestion for procurement slide:
- p95 <= 200ms at 50 concurrent users (us-west-2).
- Cost per 1k tokens <= $0.002 for q8 variant.
- Full audit logs and KMS support during tests.

Action items for us:
- Aditya: confirm whether we can bake in a quick fallback policy in the staging run (yes/no).
- Rishi: prep a short playbook for the resilient-failure scenario and available metrics.
- I’ll prepare a one-page competitive summary to send before the deep-dive.

Marissa Cole
Director, Product (Enterprise) | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
